quote: Sometimes it just it's a little it doesn't stick. But I'm sorry. Stick.
stewart_read: Rep stumbles verbally and undercuts his own credibility right after the customer flags redundant questioning — a small moment but it compounds her irritation about the call feeling careless.
coaching_implication: Coach on clean recovery lines when a customer calls out redundancy — a simple acknowledgment ('you're right, let me just confirm quickly') lands better than a stumbled excuse.

quote: Don't bother me anymore on the phone. Send me an email or send a hard copy
stewart_read: This is the schema's own acknowledged gap: the excessive_contact_complaint / channel-preference protocol is listed as TBD in Ion's schema (context.what_good_looks_like TBD list explicitly names 'excessive_contact_complaint (SESSION20 — I've gotten 45 emails)'), and this call is that exact exemplar. There is no populated canonical response for this scenario yet — Stewart flags it as raw material for that schema page rather than forcing it into an existing protocol.
alternative_hypothesis: One could read this as protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number, but that protocol addresses suspicion about how contact info was obtained, not a request to switch contact channel — the fit is wrong and should not be cited.
coaching_implication: Surface this call to Kenny as the concrete example for building out the excessive_contact_complaint / channel-preference protocol page — the manager can use this exact transcript in that calibration session.

quote: electric bill. Yeah. I can help you right now.
stewart_read: Rep talks over the customer's request and asserts he can help 'right now' instead of answering her direct ask about channel preference — a procedural miss (not honoring a stated customer preference) rather than a persuasion failure.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a legitimate attempt to keep the call moving toward the verify section, but the customer had just finished a full, explicit request — talking over her rather than answering it directly is the miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to fully acknowledge a customer's explicit request before pivoting back to his own agenda — even a one-line 'I hear you, let me explain why I still need two more things' would have preserved goodwill.

quote: List all of the ways that your company can help me lower my electricity bill or send me a hard copy in the mail. You have my address.
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the same unresolved channel-preference request. Rep's response at 01:54 ('everything we do is specific to homes') is a deflection, not an answer to whether he will or won't send something in writing.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch in the multi-touch pattern — the manager should replay this alongside the 01:12 and 02:28 instances to show the rep the full arc of the missed request.

quote: I want to send you a quote because I already have quotes from two other companies.
stewart_read: Customer discloses she already has two competitor quotes, which is exactly the kind of competitive intelligence the closer would want. Rep does not probe which companies or what was quoted; he moves straight back to his own question count.
alternative_hypothesis: The call was already deteriorating fast, so the rep may have judged there was no time left to probe — but the line was low-cost to ask and could have re-engaged her.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to catch competitive disclosures even in a tense moment — a single follow-up question ('which companies, out of curiosity?') costs seconds and gives the closer real leverage.

quote: I never said you were. I'm just saying if you want help with that, I'll goodbye.
stewart_read: The call ends on a half-sentence with no resolution offered — no confirmation of an email, no mailed info, no next step. This is a rep-owned dead end, not a customer-driven natural close.
coaching_implication: Even in a call that is clearly lost, the rep should close with an owned action ('I'll have someone email you the info today') rather than trailing off — it preserves the lead for a future touch.
